summary.headline: Chemplast Q4 FY26 net loss of INR45 crores on INR898 crore CCVL impairment; consolidated EBITDA rose to INR194 crores from INR37 crores.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 9% YoY to INR1,256 crores and EBITDA jumped to INR194 crores from INR37 crores, but the company posted a net loss of INR45 crores. The quarter absorbed an INR898 crore non-cash impairment on the investment in CCVL (suspension PVC) and a INR150 crore exceptional charge at CCVL for onerous contracts and raw material write-down. Management said suspension PVC spreads are at roughly breakeven on a replacement-cost basis because of Chinese carbide PVC imports, while specialty chemicals grew 13%. The Board also formed a committee of three independent directors to review strategic priorities, reorganisation and M&A.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals (Paste PVC, CMC, refrigerant gases)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR475 crores, up 13% YoY, with volumes up 17% YoY mainly from paste PVC; Cuddalore paste PVC ran at 100% of capacity through the year. Revenue share was 38% of Q4 total.

segments.name: Value-added Chemicals (caustic soda, chloromethanes, hydrogen peroxide)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR120 crores vs INR169 crores a year earlier (about 29% decline), with 9% share of Q4 revenue. Caustic volumes fell YoY due to membrane change at Mettur, though they improved sequentially from Karaikal.

segments.name: Suspension PVC (CCVL)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR661 crores, up 18% YoY from INR560 crores, 53% of Q4 revenue. Spreads are near breakeven on replacement cost; Chinese carbide PVC at about $820/t CFR India is pressuring prices.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the commodity business including CCVL to face a volatile near-term environment in FY27, while expecting stronger performance in specialty.
Management hopes the 7.5% customs duty on PVC returns at end-June 2026; it said this could add about $60-70 per tonne to realisations.
Anti-dumping duty on paste PVC imports from EU and Japan is expected to be implemented in H1 FY27, pending notification by the Finance Ministry.
R32 capacity expected to reach 14 kt by end of calendar 2026, with commissioning in phases through the year after the 2 kt Mettur swing plant started commercial production.
Custom manufacturing revenue target of about INR1,000 crores now expected next financial year, roughly 12 months behind plan according to Dr. Rangachari.
Management said the CCVL INR150 crore inventory write-down is expected to reverse in the current financial year.
capex_capacity: R32 refrigerant gas: 2 kt swing plant at Mettur has started commercial production; expansion to 14 kt targeted by end of calendar 2026, with design provisions for further debottlenecking.
Paste PVC at Cuddalore operated at 100% of capacity in FY26; paste PVC capacity was expanded last year.
MPB 3 Phase III expansion in custom manufacturing is progressing as planned; 45-plus molecules in the pipeline, of which 17 are commercial.
R32 quota: management said the allocation is expected by 2027, with the baseline survey running to end-2026. It is not yet confirmed.
R32 feedstock HF is covered by a couple of short-term supply tie-ups; longer-term options include the company's own support systems.
demand_pricing: Domestic suspension PVC demand fell about 1% in FY26 from roughly 4.3 million tonnes; management expects stable to marginally higher demand and a recovery one to two quarters after geopolitical stabilisation.
Chinese carbide PVC is priced around $820/t CFR India, while FOB Japan VCM lands at about $755-760/t, leaving SPVC margins at variable cost.
Paste PVC demand held steady from footwear, with healthy automotive and upholstery traction. Imports from EU declined after ADD findings.
Agrochemical slowdown led to deferred custom manufacturing sales; management says innovator demand has not been hit by generic pricing but new molecule launches are ramping more slowly.
Caustic soda prices spiked after the war began and are now normalising; chloromethane and hydrogen peroxide volumes were constrained by lower caustic output.

qa_highlights.question: Are SPVC spreads still weak and could FY27 remain stressful for CCVL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said spreads are at neutral replacement cost, with VCM prices softening slightly. It acknowledged a couple more onerous contracts hit production in May-June and called FY27 a pessimistic-case risk, while Chinese producers are also under cost pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the impairment taken and what cash-flow outlook underpins it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impairment reflects the current view with no regulatory support. At today's prices, margins are only covering variable costs; the impairment would be reviewed periodically if conditions improve.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR150 crore exceptional item and how will Q1 be affected?
qa_highlights.answer: It is the gap between actual cost and net realisable value at 31 March, expected to reverse in Q1 FY27. One or two more consignments could carry small contribution differences, and the business is roughly breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: Is the government likely to restore the 7.5% duty, and what other measures are in play?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said industry bodies are pushing for the duty to return at end-June. They are also seeking minimum import prices and QCO reinstatement; ADD is seen as the only long-term WTO-compliant solution.

qa_highlights.question: Has an ADD application on Chinese PVC been filed?
qa_highlights.answer: Not yet. Data is being compiled and filing is expected in the near future.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R32 export strategy and quota status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is working with partners on export sales; domestic and export are both planned. It expects a quota allocation by 2027 and said the baseline survey runs to end-2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the custom manufacturing and LOI-backed revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify total LOI value. Six LOIs have been signed out of 17 commercial molecules, and the INR1,000 crore target is retained for next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mandate of the independent director committee?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a broad review of portfolio reorganisation and M&A opportunities. Specialty capital allocation remains the priority, and no outcome has been predetermined.

risks_watch: Whether the 7.5% PVC customs duty returns at end-June 2026; management says this could add about $60-70/t.
ADD decision timing on paste PVC from EU and Japan (H1 FY27 expected) and filing of ADD on Chinese suspension PVC.
Further onerous contracts at CCVL hitting production in May-June; the INR150 crore reversal in Q1 depends on realisations.
Feedstock VCM availability and Middle East war effects on naphtha/ethylene and energy costs.
Quota allocation for R32 and the HF supply chain for 14 kt capacity; export partnerships still under discussion.
Outcome of the three-director committee on reorganisation and M&A; the company said it has no predetermined outcome.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious on suspension PVC, with management acknowledging uncertainty and spreads at breakeven. More confident on specialty chemicals, paste PVC and R32, though it repeatedly deferred on quantifying LOIs, ADD timing and the committee's outcome.
key_quotes: The assessment has resulted in an impairment loss of INR898 crores vis-a-vis the book value of the investments at INR1,556 crores.
It does not affect liquidity or the company's ability to operate the business.
we are positive in our specialty business, where we expect a stronger performance given the better fundamentals and prospects.
So overall, we expect that at least this time around, we are hopeful that the government will take a fair approach, and we should be able to manage the Paste business effectively.
